claims.text: A thin, compositionally tailored HEA layer can be introduced between the W and Cu phases.
The HEA interfacial layer can be formed by deposition or diffusion bonding.
Optimizing the HEA composition will enhance W–Cu compatibility.
Optimizing the HEA composition will reduce interfacial stress.
The HEA layer will act as a diffusion barrier between W and Cu.
The HEA layer will act as a stress-relief layer.
The HEA layer will accommodate thermal-expansion mismatch between W and Cu.
Diffusion-barrier and stress-relief behavior will stabilize the W–Cu interface.
Interfacial stabilization will mitigate phase separation.
Interfacial stabilization and accommodation of thermal-expansion mismatch will reduce interfacial void formation.
The compositional complexity and lattice distortion of the HEA will enhance resistance to irradiation-induced damage.
The HEA-treated W–Cu composite will have higher thermal conductivity than the untreated composite under the specified heat-transfer and irradiation conditions.
The HEA-treated composite will exhibit less interfacial void formation than the untreated composite under the specified conditions.
The HEA-treated composite will exhibit less phase separation than the untreated composite under the specified conditions.
The proposed intervention is applicable to W–Cu composites used in plasma-facing and cooling applications.
The proposed processing window is restricted to temperatures below the melting points of W and Cu.
The proposed service window includes high heat flux and irradiation.
